name: Database Migration Baseline
description: Captures business context, Factory engagement readiness, assessment inputs, constraints, governance and acceptance criteria needed to plan a database migration.

sections.title: Business Context & Scope
sections.description: Confirm the business outcome, migration boundary, workload inventory and timing.

questions.text: What is the primary business driver for this migration?
Who is the primary business owner or sponsor?
Describe the scope of this engagement, including whether application changes are included or database migration only.
Which databases, servers, schemas, applications and environments are in scope for this wave, and what is deferred?
Can the scope be divided into dependency-safe waves or subsets?
Is there a fixed migration deadline or business event driving the schedule?
questions.helpText: Include the date, event, contractual commitment, seasonal constraint or end-of-support milestone.

questions.text: Which budget, licensing or commercial constraints could affect the migration approach or target selection?

sections.title: Engagement & Delivery Model
sections.description: Set the Factory, customer and partner responsibilities before assessment or execution begins.

questions.text: Which delivery model is requested?
Which customer, partner and Microsoft teams participate, and what does each team own?
Has a RACI and scope boundary been agreed and approved?
Who can approve access, architecture, security, migration waves, cutover and final engagement sign-off?
What delivery cadence, status reporting and RAID tracking approach is required?

sections.title: Assessment Readiness
sections.description: Confirm that tool-based discovery can run safely and that its evidence will be available for design decisions.

questions.text: Who will run the assessment or metadata collection tools and return the outputs?
Has the customer security team reviewed and approved the assessment tools or scripts?
Can assessment collection run with read-only access and without exporting business or sensitive data?
Which assessment inputs are available?
options: Performance reports for representative peak periods

questions.text: List missing assessment prerequisites, access, ports, credentials or outputs and their owners.
Who will validate the dependency map, migration classification and assessment findings?

sections.title: Availability & Risk
sections.description: Define downtime tolerance, recovery objectives and operational timing constraints.

questions.text: What is the maximum tolerable downtime during cutover? (hours)
What is the Recovery Time Objective (RTO)?
What is the Recovery Point Objective (RPO)?
Describe blackout periods, peak events, batch schedules or other timing restrictions.
What annual data growth and planning horizon must the target support?
Which material migration risks or external approvals could block the target date?

sections.title: Compliance, Security & Data Governance
sections.description: Capture regulatory, data handling, retention and tool-approval requirements.

questions.text: Which compliance frameworks apply?
Which data classifications are present in the migration scope?
Are data residency, sovereignty or restrictions on data leaving the current environment applicable?
Describe retention, deletion, archival or legal-hold requirements, including data that should be archived instead of migrated.
What production-like test-data and masking requirements apply to migration rehearsals?
Which migration tools require InfoSec, procurement, DPIA or licensing approval, and what is each approval status?

sections.title: Target Platform & Connectivity
sections.description: Record the target decision, landing-zone readiness, capacity and end-to-end connectivity.

questions.text: What is the preferred target platform?
options: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines

questions.text: What criteria will decide the target and migration path for each workload?
What is the target environment readiness?
options: Landing zone ready - database not provisioned

questions.text: Are the target region, subscription, SKU, quota and regional capacity confirmed?
Who owns source-to-target network, firewall, DNS and private-connectivity approvals?
Has end-to-end connectivity and representative throughput been tested from the migration execution host?
What target operating model is expected?

sections.title: Technical Constraints
sections.description: Confirm application coupling, dependencies and remediation ownership.

questions.text: Are there applications tightly coupled to the database that must be migrated together?
List known application, reporting, identity, file, network and third-party dependencies and their owners.
Which discovered database-specific features are business-critical, removable or require remediation?
Who owns required application, schema, code and integration remediation?
Is there an existing DBA or platform team who will support migration and steady-state operations?

sections.title: Validation, Cutover & Lifecycle
sections.description: Define wave sequencing, approval evidence, hypercare and source retirement expectations.

questions.text: Will a non-production proof of concept or rehearsal precede production migration?
Who can accept data reconciliation, application behavior, performance, security and operational readiness?
Is a source and target coexistence period required after cutover?
What hypercare duration, monitoring and escalation coverage are required after cutover?
questions.helpText: The Factory service description uses five days of joint hypercare as its standard outcome.

questions.text: What evidence is required for workload validation, customer approval and final project sign-off?
What criteria and approvals are required to decommission the source and terminate related licenses or contracts?
